title: Cascaded Flow Matching for Heterogeneous Tabular Data with Mixed-Type Features
claim: A cascade first models a coarse discrete representation, then conditions a fine continuous model on it to capture mixed-type distributions.
layout: Dashed low/high-resolution regions, left-to-right arrows, stacked distribution cards on right
description: A flow diagram split by dashed boxes into Low resolution (top) and High resolution (bottom). Blue input boxes x_cat and x_num feed a purple x_low box. The numerical feature is discretized into bins C1–C5 over a density curve, and C5 is a pink NaN bin. The purple x_low box feeds an orange p_low(x_low) box. A dotted zoom-in shows bar charts of categorical probabilities p(z) and p(x_cat), with bars colored to match the bins. An orange p_high(x_num|x_low) box in the bottom row takes x_low and x_num as inputs. Arrows from both orange boxes lead to a stack of three cards on the right: Numerical, Categorical and Mixed-type Feature Distribution. The mixed-type card shows a NaN spike beside a bimodal density. Pastel fills with colored bins draw the eye first.
caption: Overview of TabCascade for the missing value generation task. We derive a categorical, low-resolution representation $\rvz$ from $\rvx_{num}$, form $\rvx_{low} = (\rvx_{cat}, \rvz)$ and then learn $p_{low}(\rvx_{low})$. We then learn the high-resolution distribution $p_{high}(\rvx_{num} | \rvx_{low})$ conditional on $\rvx_{low}$. This reduces the transport cost bound and simplifies the learning task. The discrete state $\rvz$ enables the model to naturally handle mixed-type feature distributions at generation time. This approach generalizes to arbitrary (and multiple) discrete states.
abstract: Advances in generative modeling have recently been adapted to tabular data containing discrete and continuous features. However, generating mixed-type features that combine discrete states with an otherwise continuous distribution in a single feature remains challenging. We advance the state-of-the-art in diffusion models for tabular data with a cascaded approach. We first generate a low-resolution version of a tabular data row, that is, the collection of the purely categorical features and a coarse categorical representation of numerical features. Next, this information is leveraged in the high-resolution flow matching model via a novel guided conditional probability path and data-dependent coupling. The low-resolution representation of numerical features explicitly accounts for discrete outcomes, such as missing or inflated values, and therewith enables a more faithful generation of mixed-type features. We formally prove that this cascade tightens the transport cost bound. The results indicate that our model generates significantly more realistic samples and captures distributional details more accurately, for example, the detection score improves by 51.9\%. Code is available at https://github.com/muellermarkus/tabcascade.
